We give a brief overview of the proof of Theorem 1.11 and Theorem 1.14. From a fundamental result of Gallai, we know that the subgraph D3​(G)D_{3}(G) has every block isomorphic to either an odd cycle or a clique. It is easy to see that the cliques have size at most 33, or GG is isomorphic to K4K_{4}. The first part of the proof then is to show that if any block is isomorphic to an odd cycle, then GG is isomorphic to an odd wheel. This is done by taking an odd wheel CC, deleting it, and characterizing when 33-colouring of G−CG-C extends to a (7,2)(7,2)-colouring. In the cases where we cannot extend, the neighbours of CC will form an independent set, and if GG is not a wheel, we will be able to reconfigure the colouring so that it will be able to extend to a (7,2)(7,2)-colouring.
The next part of the proof is to show that assuming we have no odd cycle blocks or K4K_{4} blocks, that every component of D3​(G)D_{3}(G) is isomorphic to a path or has at most 44 vertices. This proof follows the same themes as the odd cycle reduction. We delete vertices from D3​(G)D_{3}(G) and ask when we can extend a 33-colouring to a (7,2)(7,2)-colouring, and show that unless each component is isomorphic to a path or a claw, we can always extend.
